jobs.title: Sr. Salesforce Business Analyst
jobs.why: Very strong match for Audrey's Salesforce transformation background: business analysis, cross-functional process improvement, stakeholder work, requirements, UAT, and operational change all align closely.
jobs.gap: The senior title may expect deeper end-to-end Salesforce ownership or administration depth than Audrey has explicitly shown on her resume.

jobs.title: Senior Business Systems Analyst
jobs.why: Strong overlap with Audrey's experience translating business needs into practical system solutions, working with operational leaders and technical teams, documenting requirements, and supporting process change.
jobs.gap: The role expects independent leadership across multiple initiatives, so Audrey should emphasize ownership of transformation work and measurable delivery outcomes.

jobs.title: Business Analyst, Technology - Multiple roles
jobs.why: Technology business analysis plus Audrey's prior media-agency background makes this unusually relevant. Requirements, testing, process documentation, and cross-functional delivery are central strengths for her.
jobs.gap: The exact technology stack and team-specific requirements should be checked before applying because the listing covers multiple roles.

jobs.title: Product Analyst - Product Lifecycle Management (Quote-to-Bill)
jobs.why: Excellent bridge from business analysis into product operations. The role centers on systems, processes, lifecycle operations, and cross-functional execution, all closely related to Audrey's transformation and workflow experience.
jobs.gap: Quote-to-bill and product-lifecycle domain knowledge may be newer for Audrey, so she should connect her Salesforce workflow and process-mapping experience directly to those concepts.

jobs.title: Business Operations Analyst
jobs.why: Strong business-operations match with a useful media-tech connection to Audrey's earlier media strategy experience. Her analytics, reporting, process improvement, and cross-functional execution background should transfer well.
jobs.gap: Audrey should make the operations and analytics impact of her prior roles explicit so the move from formal BA work feels intentional rather than indirect.

jobs.title: Associate Business Analyst, Client
jobs.why: The role sits within a digital-solutions function focused on digitalization, scalability, operational efficiency, risk management, and client and employee experience. That maps well to Audrey's transformation, systems, and stakeholder background.
jobs.gap: Financial-services domain knowledge may be preferred, and the compensation suggests a high bar despite the Associate title.

jobs.title: Product Operations - Associate
jobs.why: The role is explicitly at the intersection of client operations, technology integration, and strategic execution, which is a strong match for Audrey's systems-analysis, process-improvement, UAT, and stakeholder experience.
jobs.gap: The annuities and alternative-investments domain is new, so Audrey would need to demonstrate fast domain learning and transferable operational rigor.

jobs.title: Analyst, Business Applications
jobs.why: Enterprise applications is a natural extension of Audrey's Salesforce and transformation experience. Her requirements gathering, troubleshooting, process documentation, UAT, reporting, and user-support work are directly relevant.
jobs.gap: The role may require broader enterprise-application exposure beyond Salesforce, so she should emphasize adaptability across systems and business processes.

jobs.title: Salesforce Administrator
jobs.why: Audrey's hands-on Salesforce Flow, Reports, Dashboards, Lightning, Knowledge, automation, training, and user-support work creates a credible path into a Salesforce administration role.
jobs.gap: This role may expect deeper platform administration and configuration ownership than her resume currently emphasizes, so certifications or detailed admin examples would strengthen the application.

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Analyst
jobs.why: A strong adjacent role because Audrey combines media-industry experience with CRM, reporting, analytics, and workflow improvement. Cadent's ad-tech context makes her prior media background more relevant than it would be in a generic RevOps role.
jobs.gap: Revenue-operations metrics and go-to-market ownership are not the core of Audrey's recent experience, so she should position CRM and reporting work as the bridge.

jobs.title: Associate, UX Designer - Equity Zen
jobs.why: One of the better UX-transition targets because it is an Associate-level UX role. Audrey can combine 700+ hours of formal UX training, Figma, research, prototyping, usability testing, and real enterprise UAT and user-feedback experience.
jobs.gap: The salary range starts below Audrey's $80K target and she has less direct professional UX-design tenure than candidates coming from dedicated design roles.

jobs.title: Usability Analyst
jobs.why: Strong match to Audrey's usability-testing and research training, with an additional advantage from her professional UAT, documentation, stakeholder, and user-feedback experience.
jobs.gap: The low end is below her $80K target, and a dedicated usability-research candidate may have more professional research hours.

jobs.title: User Interface Designer
jobs.why: The enterprise HR-tech and integration setting gives Audrey's business-systems background an advantage over a purely visual designer, while her UX training provides the Figma, interaction, prototyping, and design-system foundation.
jobs.gap: This is more UI-craft intensive than Audrey's recent professional work, so portfolio polish and evidence of visual design depth will matter heavily.
